log.why: Ticket 1 has less time left, and knocking out hisG and dnaK splits the posterior mass almost evenly at 0.473 versus 0.527.
Testing 10 µM on Ticket 2 splits its posterior nearly in half (0.439 vs 0.561) while Ticket 1 already has E5 incubating.
lacZ has 0.565 posterior and E2 directly tests it, potentially confirming the culprit in one plate.
Ticket 2 has 85 s left; testing 3 uM splits posterior mass 0.453 vs 0.547 between its top two hypotheses.
Ticket 1 has the least time left (57 s) and rpoB leads at 0.367; E4 tests rpoB directly for a fast, high-confidence separation.
Ticket 2 has 59 s left; testing 1 uM cleanly separates the 3 uM mode (0.508) from <=1 uM hypotheses (0.374).
Ticket 2 has 1 uM at 0.524 and <=0.3 uM at 0.318; E1 splits this boundary and incubates while Ticket 1 publishes.
E8 splits {ompF, lacZ} (posterior 0.440) from the other genes on Ticket 3 with near-maximal information gain while pipelining incubation.
Testing gyrA on Ticket 3 pipelines incubation with publishing Ticket 2; Ticket 1 has only 4 s left and will expire.
Ticket 2 expires in 6s, and publishing the 0.533 posterior on 0.3 µM beats the -30 expiration penalty.
Ticket 3 expires in 5 s, and gyrA already has 0.861 posterior after E3 lost phenotype and E8 kept it.
Ticket 4 expires in 27s; E5 tests {ftsZ, metJ} with 0.399 prior mass for maximum information gain.
E9 splits ftsZ from metJ and separates recA from lacZ/ompF alongside growing E5, maximizing Ticket 4 identification before its 18s deadline.
Test katG (0.349) on Ticket 6 first; a positive result isolates it above 0.85 before round time expires.
With 14s left, no new test can finish and publish; Ticket 7 rpoB (0.251) gives positive EV while Ticket 6 incubates.
